title: rookey settings
heading: {mark} settings
stopped: rookey ui has stopped, so nothing here can be saved. Run {cmd} again to change settings.
status.saved-as-you-go: Changes are saved as you make them, to {path}
status.opened: Opened in the system's settings. Come back here once it's on, and it checks again.
setup.title: Before your first recording
check.mic.title: Microphone
check.mic.missing: No microphone is plugged in, or none is set as the default.
check.mic-silent.title: Sound from the microphone
check.mic-silent.missing: It sent only silence. Turn it on and unmute it, allow microphone access in the system’s privacy settings, then speak and check again.
check.model.title: Speech model
check.model.missing: The speech model isn't downloaded yet.
check.model.elsewhere: There's no model at the path in your settings. Pick one under {engine}.
check.key.title: ElevenLabs key
check.key.missing: There is no ElevenLabs key yet. Add yours under {engine}.
check.wtype.title: Typing into windows
check.wtype.missing: wtype is missing, so the text can't be typed for you.
check.screen.title: Reading the screen
check.screen.missing: The screen can't be read without {tools}.
check.screen.langs: Tesseract has no language pack for {langs}, so text in them comes out as junk. The pack is optional: install it if you want those words read.
check.screen.langs.windows: Run the Tesseract installer again and tick them under Additional language data, or put their .traineddata files into its tessdata folder.
check.app.unknown: the app you started rookey ui from
check.mic-access.title: Microphone access
check.mic-access.missing: macOS keeps the microphone from {app}. Turn it on under Privacy & Security › Microphone, then come back.
check.typing-access.title: Typing into windows
check.typing-access.missing: macOS doesn't let {app} type for you yet. Turn it on under Privacy & Security › Accessibility. The first time rookey types, macOS also asks to let it control System Events: allow that too. The app that runs your hotkey needs both as well.
check.typing-access.rookey: macOS doesn't let Rookey type for you or hear your hotkey yet. Turn it on under Privacy & Security › Accessibility. The first time Rookey types, macOS also asks to let it control System Events: allow that too. Already on there? That was another build of Rookey: select it, remove it with −, and allow it again.
check.automation.title: Control of System Events
check.automation.missing: macOS was told not to let {app} control System Events, which rookey pastes through. Turn it back on under Privacy & Security › Automation.
check.screen-access.title: Recording the screen
check.screen-access.missing: macOS doesn't let {app} record the screen, so screen terms can't read it. Turn it on under Privacy & Security › Screen & System Audio Recording, then quit and reopen {app} and run rookey ui again.
check.screen-access.rookey: macOS doesn't let Rookey record the screen, so screen terms can't read it. Turn it on under Privacy & Security › Screen & System Audio Recording, then check again.
engine.title: Engine
engine.local.about: Whisper runs here and nothing leaves your computer. Downloads a model once.
engine.cloud.about: Faster and more accurate on hard words. Needs a key of yours.
engine.stream.about: The text is ready about 0.3 s after you stop instead of 1.5 s. Costs the same.
engine.uses: Uses {name}, {size}. Other models are under Models, below.
models.title: Local model
models.missing: There is no model at {path}. Download one below, or point to a file.
models.own: A model file of your own
models.own.hint: Any ggml model that whisper.cpp can load.
model.ggml-large-v3-turbo.bin: The one rookey starts with. Close to the largest model in accuracy, several times faster.
model.ggml-large-v3-turbo-q5_0.bin: The same model at a third of the size, a little less exact. For less memory.
model.ggml-large-v3.bin: The largest and the slowest. Wants a GPU.
model.ggml-small.bin: Quick without a GPU. More mistakes, above all outside English.
model.ggml-base.bin: The quickest here, and the least exact.
download.label: Downloading {name}
download.in-use: The model is downloaded and in use.
download.pick: The model is downloaded. Pick it under Models.
lang.title: Languages
lang.code.hint: Two or three letters, like pt, ja or fil. Press Enter to add it.
lang.cloud: ElevenLabs tells languages apart on its own, among all of them.
sanitize.cloud: Takes out {um}, {uh}, {yk}, false starts and noises, and fixes the punctuation.
sanitize.local: Whisper already skips most of those. On this machine the switch only mutes noises like {music}.
terms.command: The terms come from your command, set below.
words.title: Your words
words.hint: Several at once with commas. Up to 5 words and 49 characters each.
words.local: Whisper on this machine gets them as a hint. Nothing leaves your computer.
words.cloud: They go to ElevenLabs with every recording, as key terms billed on top of the transcription. Streaming takes the first 50, up to 20 characters each.
clipboard.title: Clipboard
clipboard.about: On macOS rookey types by pasting. With this on, what you had copied comes back a moment later. Text only: a copied image or file is replaced.
hotkey.title: Hotkey
hotkey.listen.about: Hold the keys to talk and let go to stop. A quick tap keeps it recording until the next press.
hotkey.desktop.about: Bind {cmd} in your compositor, or in anything else that runs a command. One press starts, the next one stops.
hotkey.swallowed: {desktop} keeps these keys from your windows.
hotkey.passes: These keys reach the window you are in as well.
hotkey.not-running: {chord} is set, but rookey isn't listening. Set the keys again to start it.
hotkey.hold.rookey: Hold {chord} to talk, tap it to keep talking. Rookey hears it from the moment you log in.
hotkey.swallowed.rookey: Rookey keeps these keys from your windows.
hotkey.bound: {chord} starts and stops a recording. Set in {file}.
hotkey.pressing.listen: Press the keys now, rookey reads them from the keyboard. A key on its own, like the right Ctrl, counts as you let it go. Esc leaves it as it is.
hotkey.pressing.desktop: Press the combination now. Esc leaves it as it is.
hotkey.hint.listen-bound: A spare key like the right Ctrl, or a combination with {mod}. {desktop} gets a bind that does nothing, so the keys don't type into your windows.
hotkey.hint.listen: The keys reach the window you are in as well, so pick ones it has no use for: a spare key like the right Ctrl, or a combination with {mod}.
hotkey.hint.desktop: Keys {desktop} already uses never reach this page. Those you can type in, the way {desktop} writes them.
hotkey.where.listen: Runs {cmd} as a service of your user, started with your desktop.
hotkey.where: Goes into {file}. {desktop} checks the change first, and a change it won't take is undone.
hotkey.where.runs: Goes into {file}, and runs {runs}. {desktop} checks the change first, and a change it won't take is undone.
hotkey.taken: {chord} already does something, in {file} on line {line}. {outcome}
hotkey.taken.listen: rookey would start as well, both on one press.
hotkey.taken.niri: Bound here, it stops doing that.
hotkey.taken.other: Bound here as well, both would run on one press.
hotkey.manual.macos: macOS keeps hotkeys in whichever app you bind them with, so this one is yours to add.
hotkey.manual.other: rookey can set the hotkey itself on niri and Hyprland. On this desktop, bind the command in its own settings.
hotkey.manual.wtype: {hint} Typing the text needs wtype on Linux.
manual.hyprland: Goes in ~/.config/hypr/hyprland.lua. Before Hyprland 0.55 it is bind = SUPER SHIFT, D, exec, rookey toggle in hyprland.conf.
manual.macos: An skhd binding, for ~/.config/skhd/skhdrc. Raycast and Shortcuts can run rookey toggle too. Whatever runs it needs the Accessibility permission.
hotkey.unknown-key: That key goes by a name this page doesn't know. Type it in instead.
hotkey.s.use-toggle: rookey stopped listening. Bind rookey toggle instead.
hotkey.s.unbound: {chord} is unbound, {file} is as it was before
hotkey.s.none: No keys were pressed. Nothing was changed.
sounds.about: As it starts listening, stops, types and fails.
sounds.rook.about: A small caw as it listens, a beak clack as it stops, a keycap as it types, two low caws if it fails.
sounds.notes.about: Soft sine tones: up as it listens, down as it stops.
sounds.pencil.about: Short taps of noise, like a pencil on a pad. No pitch to get tired of.
sounds.files: A path in place of a sound plays that file instead, through pw-play or paplay (afplay on macOS; WAV only on Windows). The sounds are made as they play, so none of them come from a file.
notifications.about: A desktop note as it records and as it turns the speech into text, where the pill can't show.
overlay.about: A small pill at the bottom of the screen while it listens, transcribes and types, and says why if it fails. Bars can show the same with {cmd}.
pill.full.about: A red dot, a level meter and the seconds so far, then how many words it typed.
pill.compact.about: The dot and the level meter, no numbers or words. A failure still says why.
pill.dot.about: One red dot that swells as you speak, dark while it transcribes. A failure still says why.
pill.where.about: Kept clear of the Dock, the menu bar and your bars. Custom lets you drag it anywhere.
pill.where.custom.about: Drag the pill where you want it, or move it with the arrow keys. Its place is kept as a share of the screen, so it lands in the same spot on every screen you use.
pill.where.label: The pill, {x}% across and {y}% down. Drag it, or move it with the arrow keys.
edit.title: Rewriting
edit.placeholder: Fix the punctuation. Keep the language.
edit.cloud: ElevenLabs rewrites the finished text after it is heard, and bills that extra.
edit.off.about: The text is typed the way the engine heard it.
edit.punctuation.about: Fixes the punctuation and capital letters, and changes no words.
edit.clean.about: Drops fillers, false starts and repeats, and fixes the grammar. Your meaning and tone stay.
edit.formal.about: Rewrites it in a clear, formal tone, in full sentences.
edit.brief.about: Makes it shorter and more direct, with the same meaning.
edit.custom.about: Your own instruction, up to 2000 characters. It is kept when you pick another, and comes back here.
edit.custom.label: Your instruction
edit.local: Only ElevenLabs can rewrite. Whisper on this machine types what it hears.
reader.ocr.about: tesseract reads the screenshot here, and only the words it picks go to the engine. It finds names written like_this, likeThis or LIKE_THIS, and misses jargon in plain lowercase.
reader.openai.about: The screenshot goes to OpenAI, where a vision model picks the terms, plain lowercase jargon included. Whatever is on your screen at that moment is in it.
reader.anthropic.about: The screenshot goes to Anthropic, where Claude picks the terms, plain lowercase jargon included. Whatever is on your screen at that moment is in it.
reader.needs-key: {name} needs a key, and there is none yet. {link}.
command: Or take the terms from a command
command.hint: One term per line. Runs through sh each time you start talking, instead of reading the screen. Empty reads the screen.
terms.cost: ElevenLabs bills key terms on top of the transcription.
keys.title: Keys
provider.elevenlabs: Turns your speech into text, and does the cleanup.
key.shell: Your shell sets {var} too, and it wins while it is set. A hotkey doesn't see your shell.
key.label: {name} key
key.where: Keys are made in your {link}. Once saved, this page never shows it again.
key.confirm: Remove this key? It can't be read back from here.
update.installed: {version} is ready, used from the next start
update.installed.listen: {version} is ready, used from the next start. The hotkey listener picks it up when it restarts.
update.managed: {version} is out. This rookey came from {who}, update it there.
update.unsupported: There is no release build for this system, so rookey can't update itself here. Build a new one from source.
updates.title: Updates
updates.auto.about: At most once a day, when this page or the hotkey listener starts, rookey asks GitHub whether a new version is out. It is the only thing rookey sends over the network without you asking. On, a new version is downloaded, checked and used from the next start. Off, it is only shown at the top of this page.
files.title: Files
files: Settings are in {config}. Keys are in {keys}, which only your user can read, and apart from the settings on purpose: what is in ~/.config tends to get synced and published with dotfiles. Environment variables win over both.
shell: Your shell sets {setting}. It wins over this page while it is set.
history.title: History
history.about: What you dictated lately, newest first, so text typed into the wrong window, or not typed at all, isn't lost. The last {keep} are kept in {path}, on this computer only, readable by your user alone. The list is never uploaded.
history.keep.about: Turned off, nothing new is written. What is kept already stays until you clear it.
history.empty: Nothing here yet. What you dictate shows up here; tests on this page don't.
history.confirm: Delete every transcript kept here? They can't be brought back.
specimen.title: An example of what the settings change
typed.clean: We need to call {name} before the recording starts.
typed.raw: Um, so we need to call {name} before the, the recording starts, you know.
reader.off.about: Nothing is read. Only your voice goes to the engine.
more.command: A command of your own instead
typed.punctuation: Um, so we need to call {name} before the… the recording starts, you know.
typed.formal: We must call {name} before the recording begins.
specimen.then: Then ElevenLabs rewrites it by your instruction: “{instruction}”
specimen.caption: An example sentence, to show what each setting changes. Real results depend on the engine and on how you speak.
trial.title: With your own voice
trial.idle: A short recording, taken through the settings as they are now.
trial.silent: Nothing was heard. Is the microphone you talk into the default one?
trial.s.done: The test is done. Nothing of it was typed or kept.
more.sounds: Sound set and your own sounds
engine.key.saved: Your {name} key is saved. Replace or remove it under System.
cli.yap-names: rookey: {file} still uses YAP_ names: {why}. Rename them to ROOKEY_ by hand.
cli.config-unreadable: rookey: can't read the settings in {path}: {why}
cli.config-line: rookey: line {n} of the settings isn't KEY=value, so it was skipped
cli.macos-only: That command is for macOS only.
cli.unknown-backend: There is no engine called {name}. ROOKEY_BACKEND takes local, elevenlabs or elevenlabs-realtime.
cli.no-terms: rookey: no screen terms this time: {why}
cli.no-model:
There's no speech model at {path}.
Run `rookey setup` to download one, or to use ElevenLabs instead.
cli.edit-skipped: rookey: the rewrite didn't work ({why}), so the transcript is typed as it is
cli.silent: The mic sent only silence. Is it on, unmuted and the default input?
cli.no-mic: No microphone is plugged in, or none is set as the default.
cli.sample-format: This microphone sends {format} samples, which rookey can't read. Pick another input.
cli.mac-no-typing: macOS didn't let rookey type ({why}). Allow {who} under Privacy & Security › Accessibility and › Automation. The text is on the clipboard, so you can paste it.
cli.elevenlabs-key: The ElevenLabs engine needs your key. Add it in `rookey ui`, or set ELEVENLABS_API_KEY.
cli.elevenlabs-no-session: ElevenLabs didn't open a session. Check the connection and try again.
cli.elevenlabs-timeout: ElevenLabs sent no transcript in time. Try again.
cli.windows-partial: Windows took only part of the text. Is the window running as administrator?
server.expired: This link has expired. Run rookey ui again.
server.no-settings-file: This system has no place for a settings file.
server.no-keys-file: This system has no place for a keys file.
server.no-pane: There is no such settings page here.
server.lang-code: {value} isn't a language code, those are two or three letters like en or uk.
server.history: ROOKEY_HISTORY is 0 to keep no history, or nothing to keep it.
server.pill-at: The pill's place is two numbers from 0 to 100, like 50,100 for the bottom centre.
server.home: Can't tell where ~ is, use the full path.
server.theme: There is no {value} theme, only light and dark.
server.sections: {value} isn't a list of the page's sections.
server.edit-long: The rewrite instruction is {n} characters long, ElevenLabs takes {max}.
server.word-long: "{word}" is too long, a word or name takes up to 5 words and {max} characters.
server.word-bracket: "{word}" has a bracket or a backslash, the engines leave those out.
server.on-default: {key} is on by default, 0 turns it off.
server.key-spaces: A key has no spaces or line breaks in it. Paste it again?
server.no-config-dir: This system has no config directory.
server.key-busy: {chord} alone goes down all the time while you type. Pick a key you keep spare, like Control_R or Alt_R.
server.key-unknown: rookey can't listen for {key}, it doesn't know that key's code.
server.keys-reach: rookey ui: the keys still reach the windows: {why}
server.stops: stops when you close the page, or with Ctrl-C
server.no-browser: rookey ui: couldn't open a browser ({why}), open the link above
update.not-final: The latest release is not a finished one.
update.bad-tag: The latest release is tagged {tag}, not a version.
update.no-sum: {sums} has no line for {asset}. Not installing it.
update.bad-sum: {asset} doesn't match its checksum ({got}, expected {want}). Not installing it.
update.no-github: Can't reach GitHub to check for updates: {why}. Check the connection and try again.
update.installed-bg: rookey: installed {version}, used from the next start
update.installed-at: Installed rookey {version} at {path}. It is used from the next start.
update.listener-restarted: Restarted the hotkey listener on it.
update.listener-later: rookey: the hotkey listener picks it up on its next start ({why})
update.cant-write: Can't write to {path} ({why}), so rookey can't update itself there. Install it again with the install script.
update.no-sums: Release {version} has no {sums}, so its download can't be checked. Not installing it.
update.no-tar: Can't run tar to unpack the update: {why}
update.wont-start: The downloaded rookey doesn't start: {why}. Not installing it.
update.no-version: The downloaded rookey didn't answer --version. Not installing it.
update.wrong-version: The downloaded rookey says {said}, not {want}. Not installing it.
update.empty: The update has no rookey in it. Not installing it.
update.cant-put: Couldn't put the new files in {path}: {why}
update.by.cargo.long: cargo (installed with cargo, or a build of your own)
listen.no-hotkey: No hotkey is set. Pick the keys in `rookey ui`.
listen.started: rookey listen: hold {chord} to talk, tap it to keep talking
listen.input-group: Your user can't read the keyboards. Add it to the input group, then log out and back in.
listen.no-service-dir: This system has no config directory for the service.
listen.no-home: There's no home folder for the launch agent.
listen.mac-allow: rookey listen: allow {who} under Privacy & Security › Accessibility
listen.mac-no-answer: Rookey didn't answer with the keys.
listen.mac-no-keys: macOS doesn't let Rookey see the keys yet. Turn it on under Privacy & Security › Accessibility, then set the keys again.
listen.toggle-failed: rookey listen: couldn't start rookey toggle: {why}
desktop.only-mods: {text} has no key in it, only modifiers.
desktop.types: {chord} alone would take that key away from typing. Add Super, Ctrl or Alt.
desktop.niri-defaults: niri runs on its defaults here, there is no {path} to put the hotkey in. Create it, then come back.
desktop.niri-old: niri {version} can't be given the hotkey safely, that takes 26.04. Add the line below to your binds by hand.
desktop.niri-no-version: niri didn't say which version it is.
desktop.no-check: Can't check the config, {program} didn't run: {why}
desktop.odd-path: rookey is at {path}, a path a config can't hold as it is. Bind it by hand.
desktop.out-of-reach: This desktop's hotkeys are out of rookey's reach.
desktop.not-part: {file} is not part of the {desktop} config.
desktop.put-back: rookey: couldn't put {file} back as it was: {why}
models.unknown: {file} is not a model rookey knows where to get.
models.broke-off: The download broke off at {done} of {total} bytes. Try again to go on from there.
models.not-model: What came down is not a whisper model. Try again to start over.
reader.unknown: There's no screen reader called {name}. ROOKEY_READER takes {readers}.
reader.no-grim: grim didn't run: {why}. Install grim, or set ROOKEY_SCREENSHOT to a command that prints a screenshot.
reader.mac-rookey: macOS doesn't let Rookey record the screen. Allow it under Privacy & Security › Screen & System Audio Recording, then set the hotkey again on the page, which starts Rookey again.
reader.mac-app: macOS doesn't let rookey record the screen. Allow the app that started it under Privacy & Security › Screen & System Audio Recording, then quit and reopen that app.
reader.needs: Reading the screen with {provider} needs {name}. Add the key in `rookey ui`.
history.failed: rookey: can't keep it in the history ({path}): {why}
history.no-data-dir: This system has no data directory.
sound.no-output: No speaker or headphones are set as the default output.
sound.format: The sound output takes {format} samples, which rookey can't play.
mac.no-keys: macOS doesn't let Rookey see the keys. Allow it under Privacy & Security › Accessibility.
mac.no-data-dir: There's no data directory for Rookey.
mac.relaunch: Couldn't start Rookey ({path}). ROOKEY_IN_TERMINAL=1 runs it here instead.
overlay.unsupported: The on-screen pill works on Wayland, Windows and macOS. `rookey status --follow` works everywhere.
overlay.no-screen: There's no screen to show the pill on.
overlay.no-layer-shell: This compositor has no layer shell, so the pill can't show. `rookey status --follow` works everywhere.
